full_judgment:
4. The prosecution case is that the prisoner was a resident of Mirpur—Section No. 12, Dacca. He collaborated with the Pakistan Occupation Army. On 8th April, 1971 at about 11 or 11-30 ann. the prisoner armed with a rifle along with three armed Pakistan Army Personnel who were also armed with rifles and some other 7/8 persons, who were variously armed with daggers and rods, entered the house of one Setab Matbar of village of Nawaberbag within Mirpur Police Station, Dacca. The prisoner along with those persons came out of the house after looting Rs. 25,000/- in cash and gold ornaments of 14 tolas. At that time Setab, who was looted, came running protesting the loot and saying why they were oppressing them. At that time Sefatullah Matbar and Ahmed Mia, two neighbors of Setab and others came to his help. The other companions of the prisoner have gone a little ahead of him. The prisoner resented their protestation and with the rifle that was in his hand shot at Setab and then fired at Sefatullah and Ahmed, one after an-other. He killed all the three persons. The party after firing some blank shots left the place. After a long time on 18-6-72 the son of Setab, Abdur Razzak lodged the First Information Report at the Mirpur Police Station. 

 There is also the evidence of P.W. 14 Maulana Mafizuddin who was Imam of Nawaberbagh at the time of the occurrence in April, 1971. He has stated that he led the Zanaza prayer of Setab Haji and Ahmed on 8th April, 1971. P.Ws. 2, 11 and 12 have also averred that they attended the Zanaza prayer, of the said deceased persons. 

 61. The learned Advocate for the prisoner has, of course cited another decision of the Dacca High Court in the case of State Vs. Nawab Ali Biswas reported in P.L.D. 1963 Dacca 61 which corresponds to 13 D.L.R. 464, where the death sentence was commuted to one of transportation for life on the ground that there was delay in the disposal of the appeal of near about three months from the date of sentence. In consideration of the length of time, the sentence was commuted to lesser one. Except this decision, the learned Advocate for the prisoner has not been able to cite any other authority on the question of delay. It is true that the delay is a ground for not inflicting the extreme sentence of death. And that will depend upon the facts and circumstances of each case and cannot be reduced to any fixed formula. In the present case the prisoner was convicted on 30th December, 1972 and we are dealing with the matter today on 24th July, 1972. Reasonable time must be allowed for the transmission of the records, service of notices, and preparation of the record of appeal and other ancillary but necessary matters before the appeal is finally heard and disposed of. Taking these factors into consideration, we do not find that the time gap is so big as to test it a long delay, so as to be a circumstances for commutation of the sentence to transportation for life.
